summary: TRAPHSE Exploration is an interactive story map that introduces school-age space fans to NASA machines left on the Moon and Mars. Learners choose a world, tap a dot, and hear a machine tell its own story: why it was sent, what it found, where it rests and what it taught us. Six machines are featured: Eagle's descent stage, the Apollo 15 rover, Surveyor 3, Sojourner, Opportunity and Ingenuity. It turns dense mission history into a friendly, accessible story for ages 10 to 14.
details: TRAPHSE Exploration is an interactive story map that teaches school-age and casual space fans about NASA machines left on the Moon and Mars. What it does and how it works: A learner picks the Moon or Mars, then taps a glowing dot on a stylised map, or a matching button. A short first-person story opens, told by the machine itself. Each story answers four questions: Why was I sent? What did I help find? Where do I rest? What did I teach? It ends with a "Did you know?" fact. Six machines are featured: Eagle's descent stage, the Apollo 15 rover, Surveyor 3, Sojourner, Opportunity and Ingenuity. Benefits and impact: It turns dense mission history into a friendly story for ages 10 to 14, so young learners connect with the engineering and the science each machine made possible. It can be used in classrooms in Ghana and elsewhere. Tools: HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single lightweight page, hosted on GitHub Pages. Atkinson Hyperlegible and Big Shoulders Display fonts (Google Fonts). Facts taken from NASA mission pages. Code and story text were drafted with an AI assistant (Claude) and reviewed and fact-checked by our team. Creativity: Each machine speaks for itself, and a blueprint-style design links the hardware's engineering to its discoveries. Factors we considered: Accuracy of every date and fact. Accessibility, with large readable text, keyboard use, light and dark modes, and a design that works on phones with slow internet. Age-appropriate language. The map is stylised and not to scale. Next steps: More machines, audio narration, a quiz and local-language versions.
